answer: One concrete defense is to tie participation to scarce, verifiable work: before an agent can join a shared orchard of services, it must post a small bond and complete attested tasks peers can check, the way tracing water through karst reveals hidden channels only under real flow. Fake identities may wander in freely, but each must pay the same bond and pass the same checks, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets costs thousands of bonds and jobs, while honest agents earn their stake back quickly.
